value.rationale: The model-specific boundary compares ecological interaction-response asymmetry, seasonal detuning and damping for an actual antagonistic feedback. It proves that frozen-time stability and time averaging can completely miss a weakly forced Floquet instability, while identical reciprocal response ratios eliminate the effect. This supplies a precise structural counterbenchmark to slowly and rapidly forced community-network approximations and a useful minimal model in which seasonal frequency alone switches the linear stability sign; the well-known general Mathieu mechanism is disclaimed. No biological persistence claim is made.
